title: Applied ML Evals: Onboarding & Regression Triage Playbook
author: Marina Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook centralizes Redwood's approach for onboarding models and datasets into the applied-ML eval ecosystem and for triaging regressions discovered during continuous evaluation. It is intended for Applied ML engineers, Evaluation owners, and Platform owners who operate the eval-harness and maintain prompt/benchmark catalogs.

Goals

- Reduce time-to-first-eval for new models from days to hours.
- Standardize prompt sets and benchmark definitions so results are comparable across models and quantization variants.
- Provide a clear, repeatable regression triage and mitigation workflow with ownership and SLAs.
- Ensure quantization/optimization changes are covered by automated regression checks.

Audience & Scope

- Audience: Applied ML engineers, release engineers, model oncall, product owners.
- Scope: Covers eval-harness onboarding, prompt set design, baseline benchmark creation, guardrail thresholds, quantization profile validation, and regression triage through remediation/rollback. Does not cover customer-specific private deployment runbooks (see eng-private-deployments).

Core Components (high level)

1) Eval Harness: The central CI-driven evaluation runner (eval-harness) that executes prompt sets, collects metrics, and uploads structured results to the eval-store.
2) Prompt Sets & Benchmarks: Canonical prompt collections, expected outputs or scoring rubrics, and metadata describing domain, coverage, and difficulty.
3) Model Onboarding Guide: Checklist and templates for registering a model, recording model metadata, and configuring eval runs.
4) Quality Guardrails: Pass/fail thresholds, regression thresholds, and business-impact tiers (P0/P1/P2).
5) Quantization Profiles: Profile definitions and validation procedures for each target hardware family.
6) Regression Triage Playbook: Step-by-step process for detection, investigation, mitigation, and postmortem.

Onboarding: Quick checklist (numbered)

1. Register model in model-catalog with required metadata: model_id, architecture, version, base_commit, owner, expected max_seq_len, tokenizer_spec.
2. Create an eval plan: select seed prompt sets (minimum: one general-purpose, one product-specific), benchmarks, and metrics.
3. Run initial baseline: execute eval-harness with 1000-sample smoke set and full benchmark (if available).
4. Record baseline artifacts: raw outputs, scoring scripts, aggregated metrics, and failure examples. Upload to eval-store.
5. Create PR for guardrail thresholds: propose SLOs and regression thresholds (example below).
6. Schedule canary rollout: tie a canary eval job to the CI pipeline and the model rollout plan.

Example model metadata (YAML snippet)

```yaml
model_id: 'llama-3b-redwood-v1'
architecture: 'decoder-only'
version: '2025-11-01'
owner: 'team-applied-ml'
max_seq_len: 2048
tokenizer: 'sacremoses-v2'
quant_profiles: ['fp16', 'int8-q4_0']
baseline_eval_id: 'eval-2025-11-01-llama-3b'
```

Prompt set & benchmark design: best practices

- Keep canonical prompt sets small, well-labeled, and single-purpose (one hypothesis per prompt).
- Include positive controls, negative controls, and adversarial variations.
- Annotate prompts with: domain, intent, difficulty, expected_behavior, scoring_method.
- Maintain a versioned prompt catalog; changes must be reviewed and linked to an eval run.

Metric guidance (examples)

- Quality: BLEU/ROUGE for structured outputs, accuracy/F1 for closed tasks, pass@k for code tasks, human-eval score for open-ended.
- Safety/regulatory: toxicity_rate, pii_detection_rate.
- Latency & cost: median_token_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, mean_tokens_per_request.

Quality guardrails and thresholds (table)

| Tier | Metric | Baseline | Regression trigger | Action 
|-----|--------|----------|-------------------|-------|
| P0  | human_eval_mean | >= 3.8/5 | drop >= 0.15 absolute | Immediate rollback + incident
| P1  | accuracy_top1 | >= 92% | relative drop >= 5% | Pause rollout + mitigation plan
| P2  | p95_latency_ms | <= 1200ms | increase >= 30% | Investigate scheduling/batching

(When adding a new model, choose appropriate tiers for each metric.)

Quantization profiles: validation matrix

- Each quant profile must include: target_hardware, quant_method, calibration_set_id, expected_quality_delta, acceptable_latency_gain.
- Mandatory validation steps:
  1) Re-run full benchmark on quantized artifact.
  2) Compare against FP baseline using pre-defined metrics.
  3) Run a small human-eval cohort on critical prompts for subjective drift detection.

Example quantization profile table (text)

Profile | Method | Target HW | Expected quality delta | Acceptable?
fp16    | none   | A100      | 0.00                 | YES
int8-q4 | symmetric | T4     | -0.03                 | YES (if within tier P1)
int8-q2 | asymmetric | CPU  | -0.12                 | NO (require mitigation)

Eval harness integration: CI patterns and commands

- CI job naming: eval/model_id/<profile>/<benchmark_version>
- Sample CI step (Bash):

```bash
# Run eval-harness for model on benchmark v3
eval-harness run --model-id llama-3b-redwood-v1 \
  --benchmark-id benchmark-general-v3 \
  --quant-profile int8-q4 \
  --out-dir /tmp/eval-outputs && eval-uploader upload /tmp/eval-outputs --store eval-store
```

- Results are expected to include: metrics.json (aggregated), raw_outputs.ndjson, scoring_logs.txt, and a small sample of human annotations if applicable.

Regression triage runbook (operational)

Detection (0-15 min):
- Alerting: automated regression detector computes rolling comparison vs baseline and fires alerts when thresholds are crossed (PagerDuty P0/P1 as configured).
- Quick validation: run targeted smoke eval (50 samples) to reproduce the regression.

Triage & assignment (15-60 min):
1) Owner picks up alert (oncall-model or model-owner).
2) Re-run failing eval with logging and higher fidelity (deterministic RNG seeds, full context).
3) Check deployment diff: model version, quant profile changes, serving runtime flags, kernel updates.

Mitigation (1-8 hours):
- If regression is caused by model artifact change: rollback to last green artifact and stop rollout.
- If caused by quantization: disable the quant profile, revert to fp16 on canary nodes.
- If caused by infra/kernel: route traffic to alternate hardware pool or fallback model variant.

Post-incident (24–48 hours):
- Postmortem with timeline, root cause, corrective actions, and owners. Publish in confluence under applied-ml-and-evals/postmortems.
- Update guardrails or expand prompt sets to cover missed scenarios.

Ownership & SLAs

- Oncall: Applied ML oncall owns first response to eval regressions. 15-minute acknowledgement SLA for P0.
- Model owners own baseline maintenance and must respond to assigned tickets within 4 hours for P1.
- Platform/Runtime own kernel and quant infra and must respond within 24 hours for P2 issues.

Rollout & Canary recommendations

- All new model releases must run canary evals before traffic-weighted rollout.
- Start with 1% traffic/0 weight to prod and run continuous evals for 24–48 hours.
- If no regressions, gradually increase to 10% then 50% while continuously monitoring eval metrics and production telemetry.

Templates & artifact naming conventions

- Baseline eval id: eval-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<model_id> (e.g., eval-2025-11-01-llama-3b)
- Quant profile id: qp-<method>-<hw>-<version> (e.g., qp-int8-q4-t4-v1)
- Benchmark id: benchmark-<domain>-v<major> (e.g., benchmark-general-v3)

Related links and references

- Eval harness standards: confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/applied-ml-eval-harness-standards-2025
- Prompt set guidelines: confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks-guidelines-2026
- Quantization best practices: confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quantization-profiles-best-practices-2026

Appendix: Quick checklist for releases

- [ ] Register model and metadata
- [ ] Baseline eval complete and uploaded
- [ ] Guardrails reviewed and approved by reviewers
- [ ] Canary eval job configured in CI and tied to rollout job
- [ ] Quantization profiles validated (if used)
- [ ] Monitoring dashboards added to per-model page

If there are questions about applying this playbook to a specific model or benchmark, open a ticket with the Applied ML team and reference the model_id and baseline_eval_id.
